Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first establish the workspace contract and inherited rollout state, then inspect both wake visual views before proposing the single candidate. I’ll use the fish-control bookshelf under the required transfer protocol and record any influence in the policy notes.

The workspace requires a pre-edit visual diagnosis and a durable guidance change; the CFD itself is explicitly out of scope. I’m now reading the inherited controller lessons, optimizer notes, and both skill protocols before touching the candidate.

The sampled set is unusually mature: all four references capture at about `18.27T`, so the “informative failure” is mechanical rather than terminal—some successful variants hit the posterior hard stop and high loads, while the velocity-conditioned barrier variants retain capture with margin. I’m separating those behaviors with compact diagnostics and the visual sheets now.

I’m applying the visual-signals-first skill now: the comparison is the slightly higher-scoring fixed-width guard (`solver_3991…`, mechanically unsafe despite capture) versus the inherited globally active stopping-distance barrier (`solver_c9eff…`, same capture route with posterior clearance). Both views on each combined sheet are being checked before any policy edit.

The visual check confirms the top-down and oblique sheets are effectively identical at sheet resolution: a coherent alternating wake persists through the same curved approach and capture, while local flow is quiescent relative to fish speed. Because three completed variants changed neither route nor termination—and one merely pre-clipped the already actuator-clipped command—the bookshelf consultation threshold is met. I’m consulting its primitive and source references now; any adopted invariant will be translated only into normalized body-frame/state feedback and logged in the required block.

The key reusable negative result is now sharp: the sampled “feasible” variant changed only the logged command columns; after removing those two columns, its entire trajectory CSV is byte-identical to the inherited barrier run and its score is identical. I’ll record that as an instrumentation boundary, then test one actual mechanism—a smooth high-demand projection that changes the applied waveform below the hard stop while leaving the terminal steering allocator and posterior viability override intact.

The single candidate is now implemented. The soft knee starts at half-envelope but asymptotes to full authority; the terminal posterior reserve branch is preserved, and the viability barrier runs afterward so safety braking can still override the soft projection. I’m invoking the required check-runner while I perform a local contract/syntax replay—no CFD will be run.

The configured check-runner could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account. I’m reading its immutable checklist and will execute the same checks directly; if the runner has repository-specific commands, I’ll use those verbatim.

The guidance check passes. The Julia contract command is blocked before policy execution because this runtime has no `julia` executable (the login profile also emits unrelated missing-SSH-file warnings). I’m checking the workspace/toolchain for a bundled Julia binary; meanwhile I’ll run the deterministic schema and boundary checks independently.

A Julia toolchain is available through the workspace’s HPC module system, so the earlier blocker is recoverable. I’ll rerun the exact lightweight policy-contract check with that module loaded, then repeat the guidance and boundary checks once more as the final check-runner pass.

The fallback checker independently confirms the guidance and boundary passes, all 19 parameter references are owned, all used observations are in contract, and a numeric emulation returns finite two-joint accelerations. The only unavailable check is Julia execution itself: the exposed Julia module is only an uninitialized launcher, and its required channel download is blocked. I’m doing one final non-CFD integrity pass over the completed files.

Produced exactly one policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) adds smooth high-demand acceleration projection while preserving terminal steering allocation and posterior viability braking.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) contains visual diagnosis, hypothesis, falsification criteria, and bookshelf transfer block.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:145) records the reusable negative lesson that duplicating downstream hard clipping changes telemetry but not dynamics.

Guidance and boundary checks pass; the deterministic schema/static finite-output checks pass. Exact Julia execution was unavailable because the installed module contains an uninitialized launcher whose channel download is blocked. No CFD was run.
